bullets.title: Pressure Cooker
bullets.note: This is a real tearjerker, a life-affirming story of a teacher in Philadelphia who trains at-risk high school students to win full scholarships to culinary school. She epitomizes the kind of tough love that I think we need more of in this country, \*especially\* in these infantilizing times. Official description: “Infamously blunt, Wilma Stephenson runs a ‘boot camp’ teaching Culinary Arts at Frankford High, disciplining her students into capable chefs and responsible students. But behind her tough exterior is a teacher who cares passionately about getting the best out of her kids.”

bullets.title: The Art of Memoir by Mary Karr
bullets.note: I’ve long been fascinated by Mary Karr ([@marykarrlit](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h0wg28/pxteh9h225o0rk/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9tYXJ5a2FycmxpdA==)), and I finally picked up her book on the craft of memoir writing after a recommendation by [Michael Pollan](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h0wg28/k5cmh6h552vqz5/aHR0cHM6Ly90aW0uYmxvZy8yMDE5LzAzLzIxL21pY2hhZWwtcG9sbGFuLXN4c3cvP3V0bV9zb3VyY2U9Y29udmVydGtpdCZ1dG1fbWVkaXVtPWNvbnZlcnRraXQmdXRtX2NhbXBhaWduPTViZg==). It applies to much of life, and I’d consider it a philosophical guide in many respects, replete with the dead serious (e.g., how to communicate past abuse) and spit-up-your-coffee funny (e.g., catshit sandwich metaphors). Highly recommended if you work with the written word in any capacity.

bullets.title: The Amazonian Travels of Richard Evans Schultes
bullets.note: This is exceptionally cool, and it captures the adventures of a real-life Indiana Jones in interactive form. I’m hoping I won’t immediately break their website. Here’s the description: “In this interactive map, explore the magical landscapes and indigenous cultures of the Colombian Amazon through the travels of the legendary ethnobotanist Richard Evans Schultes.”

bullets.section: Artist I am learning more about —
bullets.title: David Yarrow
bullets.note: ([@David\_Yarrow](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h0wg28/nqbohvhxx50p2o/aHR0cHM6Ly90d2l0dGVyLmNvbS9EYXZpZF9ZYXJyb3c=)). David Yarrow is a British fine-art photographer, financier, conservationist, and author. I recommend checking out [the wildlife category](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h0wg28/wlh2hghkkv6pmr/aHR0cHM6Ly9kYXZpZHlhcnJvdy5waG90b2dyYXBoeS9jb2xsZWN0aW9ucy1jYXRlZ29yeS93aWxkbGlmZS8=) on his website. I was recently gifted a copy of his [_Wild Encounters_ deluxe edition book](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h0wg28/0euwh9h99wr5nd/aHR0cHM6Ly9kYXZpZHlhcnJvdy5waG90b2dyYXBoeS9ib29rcy8=) (scroll down to see), and it might be the most beautiful book I’ve ever seen. It’s ENORMOUS, the craftsmanship is incredible, and the price tag is suitably high (~£1,500!). If you love his art but prefer something smaller and less car-down-payment, I recommend checking out the [non-deluxe option](https://el2.fourhourmail.com/c/75u8wd0mmu8h0wg28/8oiqhoh22pnvwl/aHR0cHM6Ly9kYXZpZHlhcnJvdy5waG90b2dyYXBoeS9ib29rcy8=) at the top of that same page.
